data.title: Add epic bugs for multi-step features
data.body:
## Goal

Add "epic" bugs that contain ordered sub-bugs representing sequential steps to ship a feature.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docket epic "Feature name"` creates an epic bug (new type/flag)
- [ ] `docket new "Step description" --epic EPIC_ID` creates child with auto-numbered suffix
- [ ] Children get suffixed IDs: `abc1.1`, `abc1.2`, `abc1.3` (auto-increment)
- [ ] `docket epic EPIC_ID` shows epic detail with step progress
- [ ] `docket list` shows epics with `[2/5]` style progress indicator
- [ ] `docket work EPIC_ID` automatically works on current (next incomplete) step
- [ ] Epic auto-closes when final step is marked done
- [ ] `docket ready` considers epics (shows next step of highest priority epic)

## Design

### ID Scheme
- Epic: regular 4-char ID (`abc1`)
- Children: parent ID + `.N` suffix (`abc1.1`, `abc1.2`)
- Suffix auto-increments on creation

### Storage
- Epic: `.docket/bugs/abc1.jsonl` with `Created` event that has `is_epic: true`
- Children: `.docket/bugs/abc1.1.jsonl`, `.docket/bugs/abc1.2.jsonl`
- New event type: `EpicChildCreated { parent_id, order }` in child's log
- Or: track in parent with `ChildAdded { child_id, order }`

### Status Derivation
Epic status is derived from children:
- No children started → epic is Approved (or Draft if not approved)
- Any child InProgress → epic is InProgress  
- All children Done → epic is Done
- Display shows `[completed/total]` count

### Display

List view:
```
ID    STATUS      PRIORITY  TITLE
abc1  [2/3]       high      Add user authentication
def1  [4/7]       medium    Refactor payment system
ghi1  approved    low       Fix typo in docs
```

Epic detail (`docket epic abc1`):
```
Epic abc1: Add user authentication (2/3 complete)

  ✓ abc1.1  Done        Design auth schema
  ✓ abc1.2  Done        Implement login endpoint  
  → abc1.3  InProgress  Add session management      ← current
```

### Workflow
1. Create epic: `docket epic "Add auth"`
2. Add steps: `docket new "Design schema" --epic abc1`
3. Approve epic: `docket approve abc1` (approves all children? or just epic?)
4. Work: `docket work abc1` → works on abc1.1 (first incomplete)
5. Complete: `docket done abc1.1` → moves to abc1.2
6. Repeat until all steps done
7. Epic auto-transitions to Done

### Edge Cases
- Adding steps to an epic that's partially complete (allowed, appends to end)
- Reordering steps (probably not supported initially)
- Skipping steps (warn but allow?)
- Working on non-current step (allow with warning?)

## Context

Epics answer: "What big features are in flight and where are they in the lifecycle?"

The sequential numbering (`.1`, `.2`, `.3`) communicates workflow order - these steps are meant to be done in sequence. The progress indicator (`[2/5]`) gives at-a-glance status.

This differs from dependencies (which are blocking relationships) and tags (which are just grouping). Epics are ordered pipelines.

## Log
